_about: Findings this project has examined and accepted. Read by the local code
Matching is file + rule_id, never line number, so edits above a line do
not silently un-suppress it. Every entry needs a 'reason'; 'doc' should
point at the project's own write-up rather than paraphrasing it here.

accepted.reason: Public installed-app OAuth client secret, embedded on purpose. An installed/desktop app has no server to keep a secret on, so Google issues Desktop-app credentials whose secret is explicitly 'not treated as confidential'; the same value is published in Google's own Gemini CLI source. The sensitive artifact is the user's token, which lives at 0600 under ~/.config, outside the repo. Kept visible with an explanatory comment rather than obfuscated, and pushed via GitHub's unblock-secret acknowledgement so the decision is auditable.
Same accepted value as the generic-api-key entry, reported by gosec instead of gitleaks. Both need an entry because matching is per rule_id.
Same installed-app OAuth client secret rationale as gemini_oauth.go: public by necessity, harmless without a stolen user token.
Same accepted value, reported by gosec instead of gitleaks.
Test fixture. The key-shaped string exists so the endpoint-hygiene test can prove such values are handled correctly. Not a live credential.
The flagged literal is the sentinel string "oauth-login" assigned to Provider.APIKey to mark 'this provider authenticates by OAuth, not by key'. A mode marker, not a credential.

gosec taint analysis treats os.UserHomeDir()/os.UserConfigDir()/XDG_CONFIG_HOME as attacker-controlled. Here they are joined with constant literals to locate this app's own config. Anyone able to set XDG_CONFIG_HOME for this process already controls the account that config belongs to, so no privilege boundary is crossed.
